source.title: Geodesic Flow Kernels for Semi-Supervised Learning on Mixed-Variable Tabular Dataset

algorithm_steps.description: Input tabular data containing mixed continuous and categorical variables.
Apply variable-specific corruption methods: Hard corruption for continuous variables and Soft corruption for categorical variables to generate corrupted views.
algorithm_steps.source_span: Abstract; Methodology (Continuous Variable Corruption; Categorical Variable Corruption)

algorithm_steps.description: Generate feature representations for the corrupted inputs using MLP heads.
Compute subspace bases via PCA on the feature representations.
Calculate Geodesic Flow Kernel (GFK) based similarity measure between the subspaces of corrupted inputs to capture geometric changes.
Generate tree-based embeddings from labeled data to leverage hierarchical relationships.
Compute Geodesic similarity loss for unlabeled data and Cross-entropy loss for labeled data.
Optimize model parameters by minimizing the combined loss function.
Predict labels for test data using the trained classifier.

assumptions.name: mixed_variable_types

assumptions.name: semi_supervised_setting
assumptions.description: The learning setting is semi-supervised, involving both labeled and unlabeled data.

assumptions.name: geometric_structure
assumptions.description: Geometric changes between corrupted inputs on the Grassmann manifold are informative for learning.

data_requirements: Mixed-variable tabular dataset with continuous and categorical features.
Subset of labeled data for supervised loss and tree-based embedding.
Unlabeled data for consistency regularization via geodesic flow kernels.

mathematical_specification.objective: Minimize combined loss of Geodesic similarity loss (unlabeled) and Cross-entropy loss (labeled).
mathematical_specification.decision_rule: Classification based on the output of the MLP head classifier.
mathematical_specification.estimator: Semi-supervised classifier using Geodesic Flow Kernels and Tree-based embeddings.

implementation_components.description: Variable-specific corruption: Hard corruption for continuous variables (permuted features emphasized) and Soft corruption for categorical variables (mixed with permuted features).
